title: Quantum vs Classical Cryptography
description: One-time pads, RSA, Shor and Grover, and information-theoretic security

questions.question: In classical cryptography, the main task of an encryption algorithm is to
options: convert a plaintext into a ciphertext that cannot be read without the key
make the ciphertext the same length as the plaintext
authenticate the sender of the message
compress the message to reduce its storage size
questions.correctAnswer: convert a plaintext into a ciphertext that cannot be read without the key

questions.question: The Vernam one-time pad achieves perfect secrecy only if
options: the key is truly random, at least as long as the message, and never reused
the key is a secret but short string that is easy to distribute
the key is derived from the plaintext with a secure hash function
the key is reused many times but is kept confidential forever
questions.correctAnswer: the key is truly random, at least as long as the message, and never reused

questions.question: Why is the one-time pad perfectly secure?
options: every plaintext of that length is consistent with the same ciphertext, so the ciphertext carries no information about the plaintext
the encryption algorithm is faster than any known classical attack
the key is stored inside a tamper-resistant hardware module
the key can only be computed from the ciphertext with great difficulty
questions.correctAnswer: every plaintext of that length is consistent with the same ciphertext, so the ciphertext carries no information about the plaintext

questions.question: The main practical weakness of the one-time pad is
options: the difficulty of distributing a key as long as the message
the slowness of the encryption operation
its vulnerability to frequency analysis
its reliance on a shared secret key
questions.correctAnswer: the difficulty of distributing a key as long as the message

questions.question: Frequency analysis breaks classical substitution ciphers because
options: the ciphertext preserves the statistical frequencies of the plaintext symbols
the cipher key is usually a word taken from a dictionary
the cipher is a linear map that Gaussian elimination inverts
the ciphertext is always shorter than the plaintext
questions.correctAnswer: the ciphertext preserves the statistical frequencies of the plaintext symbols

questions.question: Public-key cryptography solves a problem that symmetric cryptography cannot solve by
options: allowing two parties to establish a shared secret over a public channel, with no prior private key exchange
removing the need for randomness in key generation
making the encryption one-time and information-theoretically secure
eliminating the need for authentication certificates
questions.correctAnswer: allowing two parties to establish a shared secret over a public channel, with no prior private key exchange

questions.question: The security of RSA rests on
options: the practical difficulty of factoring a large product of two large primes
the difficulty of computing discrete logarithms
the one-wayness of a cryptographic hash function
the unpredictability of a randomly chosen prime
questions.correctAnswer: the practical difficulty of factoring a large product of two large primes

questions.question: Which statement about RSA key sizes is correct?
options: larger moduli make factoring harder, which is why recommended RSA key sizes have grown over the decades
larger moduli make factoring easier because more candidate factors become available
RSA key size has no influence on the security of the scheme
RSA with a 2048-bit modulus is already known to be broken and cannot be deployed
questions.correctAnswer: larger moduli make factoring harder, which is why recommended RSA key sizes have grown over the decades

questions.question: Shor's algorithm threatens public-key cryptography because it
options: factors large integers and computes discrete logarithms in polynomial time on a quantum computer
searches an unsorted list of $N$ items in $\sqrt{N}$ steps
simulates a large classical computer exactly, with no advantage of its own
brute-forces a symmetric key faster than Grover's search can
questions.correctAnswer: factors large integers and computes discrete logarithms in polynomial time on a quantum computer

questions.question: Grover's algorithm improves unstructured search over $N$ candidates by
options: reducing the number of queries from about $N$ to about $\sqrt{N}$
reducing the number of queries to a polynomial in $N$
giving a constant-factor speedup of exactly $2$
increasing the number of required queries by a factor of $\sqrt{N}$
questions.correctAnswer: reducing the number of queries from about $N$ to about $\sqrt{N}$

questions.question: If Grover's algorithm is applied to a $k$-bit symmetric cipher key, the effective brute-force security becomes
options: roughly $2^{k/2}$ candidate keys, i.e. about $k/2$ bits of security
roughly $2^{2k}$ candidate keys, i.e. $2k$ bits of security
unchanged at $2^k$ candidates, since Grover's algorithm needs the key to be public
negligible, because Grover's algorithm breaks any symmetric cipher in a few thousand operations
questions.correctAnswer: roughly $2^{k/2}$ candidate keys, i.e. about $k/2$ bits of security

questions.question: The usual response to Grover's algorithm is to
options: double the symmetric key length, for example moving from AES-128 to AES-256
switch to a one-time pad of the same key length
replace random keys with a fixed key agreed once and used forever
reduce the block size of the cipher
questions.correctAnswer: double the symmetric key length, for example moving from AES-128 to AES-256

questions.question: A cipher is said to be information-theoretically secure when
options: the information an eavesdropper can obtain is bounded by a computable quantity no matter how much computing power is used
breaking it would require more computing power than is available today
the algorithm has been formally proven free of implementation errors
the key is long enough to make brute force impractical
questions.correctAnswer: the information an eavesdropper can obtain is bounded by a computable quantity no matter how much computing power is used

questions.question: In its ideal form, quantum cryptography differs from classical public-key cryptography because its security
options: follows from the laws of physics rather than from the current difficulty of a computational problem
uses much longer keys than any classical scheme
allows information to be transmitted faster than light
requires no generation of random numbers at all
questions.correctAnswer: follows from the laws of physics rather than from the current difficulty of a computational problem

questions.question: A quantum channel allows something a classical channel cannot, namely
options: transmitting a quantum state whose measurement statistics can reveal interception
faster-than-light transfer of information
unlimited bandwidth regardless of the distance involved
simultaneous transmission to an unlimited number of recipients
questions.correctAnswer: transmitting a quantum state whose measurement statistics can reveal interception

questions.question: A QKD system actually produces
options: a shared secret key, which the users then use with a conventional cipher
the plaintext message itself, delivered without any classical cipher
a digital signature certifying the sender's identity
a quantum computer that performs the encryption
questions.correctAnswer: a shared secret key, which the users then use with a conventional cipher

questions.question: In QKD, the classical channel is required to be authenticated so that
options: an eavesdropper cannot impersonate one of the two parties during the public exchange of bases and error data
the key material itself can be sent over the classical channel
the two parties can certify that their devices have not been tampered with
the measured error rate can be driven below the security threshold
questions.correctAnswer: an eavesdropper cannot impersonate one of the two parties during the public exchange of bases and error data

questions.question: Why is QKD expected to resist attacks by future quantum computers while RSA does not?
options: QKD security is based on physical principles rather than computational hardness, and can be proven secure even against unbounded computation
QKD keys are additionally encrypted with a quantum-resistant cipher
QKD networks are isolated from the public internet
QKD devices can detect and automatically reverse any quantum attack
questions.correctAnswer: QKD security is based on physical principles rather than computational hardness, and can be proven secure even against unbounded computation

questions.question: Which statement about the difficulty of integer factoring is correct?
options: no polynomial-time classical algorithm is known, but Shor's algorithm provides one on a quantum computer
factoring large integers is easy classically but slow on a quantum computer
factoring is already in polynomial time classically, so quantum computers add nothing
factoring is proven to require time exponential in the number of digits
questions.correctAnswer: no polynomial-time classical algorithm is known, but Shor's algorithm provides one on a quantum computer

questions.question: Quantum computers threaten the Diffie-Hellman key exchange through
options: Shor's algorithm applied to the discrete logarithm problem
Grover's search over the group elements
brute force over a small number of pre-shared values
measurement-induced collapse of the shared secret
questions.correctAnswer: Shor's algorithm applied to the discrete logarithm problem

questions.question: Post-quantum cryptography differs from quantum cryptography because it
options: runs on ordinary computers using classical algorithms designed to resist quantum attacks
uses the same qubit hardware as QKD systems
guarantees information-theoretic security against every future attack
transmits key material over quantum channels
questions.correctAnswer: runs on ordinary computers using classical algorithms designed to resist quantum attacks

questions.question: A source of true unpredictability is essential in quantum key generation because
options: predictable basis choices would let an adversary know which measurements to make in order to avoid detection
a deterministic generator cannot be implemented in hardware
quantum measurement always consumes randomness as a resource
classical random number generators are far too slow to keep up with the qubit rate
questions.correctAnswer: predictable basis choices would let an adversary know which measurements to make in order to avoid detection
